Study-level balance spread across propensity models

Source: R/balance_spread.R
balance_spread.Rd

For each model, the model's MatchIt weights from match_each_model() are passed to cobalt and four balance statistics are computed:

  • smd_max_main: maximum absolute standardized mean difference over the main terms;

  • smd_max_extended: the same over main terms plus squares and 2-way interactions (cobalt::bal.tab(int = interactions, poly = polynomial));

  • energy_distance: cobalt::bal.compute() with stat = "energy.dist";

  • ks_max: cobalt::bal.compute() with stat = "ks.max".

Usage

balance_spread(
  match_set,
  treatment,
  covariates,
  interactions = TRUE,
  polynomial = 2,
  use_gate = TRUE,
  models = NULL
)

# S3 method for class 'balance_spread'
print(x, ...)

Arguments

match_set

A match_set from match_each_model().

treatment

The 0/1 treatment vector, in the data's row order; must equal the treatment stored in match_set.

covariates

A data frame with one row per patient, in the data's row order. Factors are split into dummies by cobalt; character columns are an error.

interactions

TRUE (default) to include all 2-way interactions in smd_max_extended.

polynomial

Highest power of the continuous covariates in smd_max_extended (default 2, squares).

use_gate

TRUE (default) to compute the spread over the models that passed the log-loss gate; FALSE to use every model.

models

Optional character vector of model ids to use instead of a gate; it overrides use_gate. The wrapper propensity_sensitivity() passes the final quality-gate set (log-loss and balance) this way.

x

A balance_spread object.

...

Not used.

Value

An object of class "balance_spread": a list with models (one row per model: model_id, in_use, smd_max_main, smd_max_extended, energy_distance, ks_max), spread (one row per statistic: statistic, range, sd, worst_value, worst_model), summary, models_used, quality_gate_left_fewer_than_two_models and settings.

Details

The spread of each statistic over the models in use is its range (max - min), its standard deviation, and the worst (largest) value with the model that produced it. The table of models lists every model of the match set with an in_use column, so that the balance part of the quality gate can read every model; the spread uses the models in use only. The oracle entry and the bootstrap block are never used.

cobalt settings (verified against cobalt 5.0.0)

estimand = "ATT", method = "matching", s.d.denom = "treated": the standardization uses the standard deviation of the treated group in the unweighted sample. binary = "std" and continuous = "std": binary covariates are standardized as well (cobalt's bal.tab() default for binary covariates is the raw difference in proportions, while bal.compute(stat = "smd.max") standardizes them; the package uses the standardized version throughout so the two agree). Example: on lalonde after the logistic match with replacement, married has a raw difference in proportions of 0.059 and a standardized difference of 0.152, so the choice decides whether a 0.10 balance threshold is met. Weighted means, the energy distance and the KS statistics do not depend on how the weights of the untreated patients are scaled.

Quality gate

With use_gate = TRUE only the models that passed the log-loss gate are used. If fewer than two passed, all models are used and quality_gate_left_fewer_than_two_models is TRUE . The flag reports the gate's outcome whatever use_gate is.

Examples

data("lalonde", package = "MatchIt")
model_set <- fit_propensity_models(
  treat ~ age + educ + race + married + nodegree + re74 + re75,
  data = lalonde, seeds = 1, n_trees = 100,
  algorithms = c("logistic_regression", "random_forest", "gradient_boosting")
)
match_set <- match_each_model(model_set, lalonde, replace = TRUE)
covariates <- lalonde[, c("age", "educ", "race", "married", "nodegree", "re74", "re75")]
balance <- balance_spread(match_set, lalonde$treat, covariates)
balance

#>    gradient_boosting_1   TRUE       0.2854           0.3769         0.08851
#>  ks_max
#>  0.3568
#>  0.1405
#>  0.1351
#> Spread over the models in use:
